| Invalid | Commands that can contact MCPJam exit `2` (`MANAGED_SETTINGS_INVALID`), naming the file and the problem. Nothing is sent to MCPJam or its telemetry. Other commands still run. |

The file is invalid when it is not JSON, when `version`, `apiUrl` or `lock` is missing or has the wrong type, when `version` is not `1`, when it has any other key, when it cannot be read, when `apiUrl` has credentials, a query or a fragment, or when `apiUrl` uses plain `http://` to a host other than a loopback address.

## Saved logins and API keys

| Situation | Result |
--
| Destination | While locked |
| - | - |
| The locked MCPJam server (API, CLI login settings) | Allowed |
| Any other MCPJam server address | Refused before any request |
| A redirect (`3xx`) in answer to an MCPJam API request | Refused, locked or not (`BACKEND_REDIRECT_REFUSED`, exit `2`) |
| URLs the locked server returns (model leases, artifact downloads, tunnel relay) | Allowed: your server chose them |
| The sign-in provider your server's login settings name | Allowed |
| Model providers, MCP servers under test, the local Inspector | Not governed |
| MCPJam telemetry and the npm update check | Off |

`--api-header` values, for an edge authenticator in front of your server, are sent on MCPJam API requests and the CLI login settings request only. They never go to the sign-in provider or follow a redirect.
--
## Corporate proxy

When `HTTPS_PROXY` or `HTTP_PROXY` is set (either case), the CLI process sends its `fetch` requests through the proxy and honors `NO_PROXY`: MCPJam's API, model providers and MCP servers over HTTP. `HTTPS_PROXY` covers `https` destinations and `HTTP_PROXY` covers `http` ones; with only `HTTP_PROXY` set, `https` requests use it too. `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` always connect directly, so local MCP servers and the local Inspector keep working. A value without a scheme, such as `proxy.corp.com:8080`, means `http://`; a value that is not an http(s) URL is ignored with a warning. Two connections do not use the proxy yet: the relay connection of `mcpjam cloud tunnel` and the `mcpjam oauth` debugging proxy.

The update check runs in a separate short-lived process that uses Node.js's own proxy support. On Node.js older than 22.21, or 24.x older than 24.5, the check is skipped while a proxy is set rather than sent directly.

For a TLS-inspecting proxy or a private CA, trust its root certificate the Node.js way: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/ca.pem`, or, on Node.js 22.15 or later, `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca` to use the system store; older releases refuse to start with that option. Set either in the environment the CLI starts in.
